Immigrate

IM-uh-grayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To immigrate to come to live permanently in a foreign country.

During the nineteenth century, millions of people chose to immigrate across the Atlantic in search of factory work and open farmland.

Worked Example

Many scientists immigrated to the United States in the mid-twentieth century, drawn by new research opportunities and funding.

Immigrate means to move permanently into a new country to live there -- always describing the arrival, from the new country's point of view.

How Immigrate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

relocate

relocate: to move to a new place to live

resettle

resettle: to establish a new, permanent home somewhere

Antonyms

emigrate

emigrate: to leave one's own country to live elsewhere -- the same move, described from the country being left

repatriate

repatriate: to return someone to their own native country

How Strong Is It? — visit → naturalize → immigrate

visit vs. immigrate

visit vs. immigrate: To visit is to make a brief, temporary stay with no intention of staying permanently, unlike immigrating.

naturalize vs. immigrate

naturalize vs. immigrate: To naturalize is to formally become a full legal citizen of a new country, an even more permanent step than simply immigrating.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of immigrate.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im- / in-

prefix — im- / in-: into, toward (Latin)

root — -migr-

root — -migr-: to move, to journey (Latin migrare)

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make or do; forms a verb (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin in- ('into') plus migrare ('to move') plus the verb suffix -ate: literally 'to move into.' The same migr- root gives migrate and emigrate (e-, 'out of') -- the same journey, named from the opposite end.

Use the root in a new word: migratory

Use the root in a new word: migratory: The migratory birds returned to the lake every spring, retracing the same path their ancestors had flown for generations.

Root Check

Word Choice

Immigrate and emigrate (which you already learned) describe the exact same move -- you emigrate FROM your home country and immigrate TO the new one -- so the prefix tells you which direction the story is being told from.
